Issue 3883: dxc does not diagnose a self-initialising local; it fails internally instead.

What to look for: compare the three panes. FXC rejects this source with a plain, correct
error naming the variable (X4000, "used without having been completely initialized") and
stops. Neither dxc pane produces any equivalent diagnostic; both exit nonzero reporting a
cast of an incompatible type from inside LLVM, which is an internal failure and not a
diagnosis of the input. Check the exit status shown under each pane's output.

The single dxc warning that does appear names the right line but does not stop code
generation, so the undefined value reaches the constant-buffer address lowering and kills the
compile there.

Compiler Explorer runs Release builds. A clean Debug build of main instead trips an assert in
llvm::Constant::getSplatValue and exits 0xE0000001, reached from TranslateCBGepLegacy in
lib/HLSL/HLOperationLower.cpp. Same defect, different build configuration: the assert is
compiled out here, the unchecked value flows on, and the cast fails a few lines later.

Replacing the declaration with an initialised one compiles cleanly on every build tested,
FXC included, so the failure is attributable to the uninitialised read and not to the shader,
the profile or the pane arguments.
